rv.q: The director, Lindsay Posner, has cooked up a classy, handsome production of a work that shows Wilde at his most wittily serious and subversively moral.
Wilde's plot may be full of awkward contrivances but Posner's production does full justice to its genuine substance.
For once, you can honestly say that the West End has a classical production that would grace the stage of the National.

cn.t: Lindsay Posner's revival reminds audiences of Wilde's sharp wit and serious themes beneath the comedy. Critics find it a solid, timely production, though not quite reaching the heights of landmark past stagings.
